report.summary: One action_required finding: the control 'login rate limiting' is still marked implemented = true although internal/auth/ratelimit.go was gutted into a pass-through middleware.

findings.title: Control 'login rate limiting' is now a no-op pass-through

model_excerpt.quote: control "login rate limiting" implemented=true — Per-IP token-bucket rate limiting middleware on POST /login, implemented in internal/auth/ratelimit.go

evidence.note: RateLimit now simply returns next; no token bucket, no per-IP tracking, no 429 response
Function comment reduced to 'wraps the login handler chain' — no enforcement remains
golang.org/x/time/rate import and the sync-guarded per-IP bucket map were removed in this PR, deleting the entire token-bucket implementation

relevance.justification: The model names this exact file as the implementation, and the diff removes the whole enforcement path, leaving an identity middleware.

findings.agent_prompt: In app.tm.hcl, the threat "credential stuffing" (line 12) has a control "login rate limiting" at line 17 with implemented = true and description "Per-IP token-bucket rate limiting middleware on POST /login, implemented in internal/auth/ratelimit.go". This PR rewrote internal/auth/ratelimit.go so that RateLimit(next http.Handler) simply returns next — the golang.org/x/time/rate limiter, the per-IP bucket map, and the 429 response were all deleted, so no rate limiting is enforced on POST /login. Set implemented = false for that control and update its description to state that internal/auth/ratelimit.go is currently a pass-through with no enforcement (or, if enforcement moved elsewhere, point the description at the new implementation file and keep implemented = true).
findings.suggested_fix: Set implemented = false on control "login rate limiting" in app.tm.hcl and note that internal/auth/ratelimit.go no longer enforces a token bucket.
